oliver: Quick heads-up: found a race where rotating keys mutates shared aiohttp session headers and leaks into other clients.
oliver: Repro: two AsyncClient instances using reuse_http_session=True with different api_keys. After rotate on provider A, some requests from client B show A_new in Authorization.
jin: can you paste the smallest repro you have? interested if this only happens with our EnvCredentialProvider or any provider.
oliver: minimal example below, seen in our integration test harness.
oliver: ```py
# simplified repro
from redwood import AsyncClient, EnvCredentialProvider
import asyncio

prov = EnvCredentialProvider()  # test sets KEY_A and KEY_B
client_a = AsyncClient(api_key=prov.for_env('KEY_A'), reuse_http_session=True)
client_b = AsyncClient(api_key=prov.for_env('KEY_B'), reuse_http_session=True)

prov.rotate_env('KEY_A', 'KEY_A_NEW')
# many concurrent calls from client_b
await asyncio.gather(*(client_b.generate('ping') for _ in range(40)))
```
oliver: server logs: ~25% of client_b requests had Authorization: Bearer KEY_A_NEW.
fatima: sounds like middleware is doing session.headers.update(...) instead of injecting per-request headers. that's a no-no for shared sessions.
jin: agree. quick fix: set header per request or clone session headers before mutate. can we add a unit test that simulates concurrent rotate + requests?
oliver: temp workaround for customers: set reuse_http_session=False when you expect key rotation. but that's not ideal.
fatima: I'll file an issue and add tests + fix in auth middleware. also check any global singletons in credential provider caching.
oliver: created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4281 (repro attached).
ops-bot: Issue #4281 created and assigned to @fatima. Priority: P2. ETA: sprint-23.
jin: thanks. once there's a patch please include a perf note; we added session-level headers for perf reasons. prefer a fix that preserves performance but avoids mutation.
oliver: will follow up with traces from the customer and a small dockerized repro. thanks all.
